summary: Verified mathematical dossier for “The third rhythm”: a 94-second, single-world 3D explanation of TOI-4342’s 18.9082-day candidate, with implementable geometry and explicit evidence limits.
content:
Reverse prerequisites: “A third planet?” depends on “Repeated dimming”, “Orbit + sightline”, and “Rule out impostors”. These require “Light + blocked area”, “Period + phase”, and “Projection + inclination”. Place the dependency graph in depth, illuminate its connections backward, then teach forward. Connections express prerequisites, not independent proofs.

Definitions and hypotheses: Flux F is received light per unit time; a transit is a foreground body overlapping the stellar silhouette along a specified sightline. Rstar and Rp are radii; k=Rp/Rstar; δ=(Fout−Fin)/Fout. Period P is recurrence time; phase is position within a cycle. Inclination i is the angle between orbital normal and sightline: i=90° is edge-on. Impact parameter b is the minimum projected center separation divided by Rstar; distinguish this symbol from planet b. Assume opaque spherical bodies, negligible planetary light/mass, and circular illustrative orbits. Uniform surface brightness is a teaching approximation; limb darkening and contaminating light alter real transit depths.

Host and established planets: TOI-4342 / TIC 354944123 has approximately Mstar=0.63 Msun, Rstar=0.60 Rsun, Teff=3900 K, distance 61.54 pc. Retain the original radii 2.266 and 2.415 Rearth. Tey’s team validated the two transiting planets using photometry, spectroscopy and imaging; their results do not validate the new signal. [Tey et al. 2023](https://arxiv.org/html/2301.01370v1). Use supplied periods Pb=5.5382498 d and Pc=10.688716 d. The separate 47.5-day, probably non-transiting ESPRESSO RV candidate is not this 18.9082-day signal; omit its orbit. [Parc et al. 2026](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.22115).

Blocked-area derivation: For uniform projected intensity I, Fout=IπRstar² and blocked flux=IπRp² when the smaller disk is entirely inside the stellar silhouette. Thus δ=k², independent of where that fully interior disk lies. The film’s sole main displayed formula is δ≈(Rp/Rstar)²≈0.001142, with “Uniform-disk illustration” and “About 1142 parts per million”. This follows the standard transit geometry. [Seager & Mallén-Ornelas, equations 1–4](https://arxiv.org/html/astro-ph/0206228). Use k=0.033789403644782876 from transit_fit.json: k²×10⁶=1141.7237986700663, exactly reproducing its stored depth. This identity is not independent photometric confirmation.

Implementable geometry: Center the star at the origin; choose the physical observer toward +z. The stellar surface is S(u,v)=Rstar(sin u cos v,sin u sin v,cos u), u∈[0,π], v∈[0,2π]. The planet is r(t)+kS(u,v). Reuse these meshes. Meridians and latitude curves are parameter restrictions of S. The stellar surface is S²; its visible silhouette bounds a disk, not a sphere. Project along the observer’s sightline with Π(x,y,z)=(x,y,0). A geometric overlay can use D(s,v)=Rstar(s cos v,s sin v,0), s∈[0,1]; keep it attached to the star in the 3D world. Shaded mesh brightness is not a photometric calculation.

For an inclined circular orbit, r(θ)=a(sin θ,cos i cos θ,sin i cos θ), θ∈[0,2π], with θ=0 at foreground conjunction. Its normal is (0,−sin i,cos i); its path is S¹. The orthographic projection has semiaxes a and a|cos i|, degenerating to a line when edge-on. The physical orbit remains circular. Foreground transit requires z>0 and projected separation d<Rstar+Rp. Behind the star the planet remains present, becoming visible from another camera direction; do not delete it. Keep the physical observer marker distinct from the moving explanatory camera.

Transit closeup: Set Rstar=1, Rp=k and b=0.7468945703. The projected stellar chord y=b has x∈[−0.66494248,+0.66494248]. This is a projected chord, not the planet’s full 3D trajectory. Since b+k=0.780684<1, the disk is fully interior at mid-transit. At any foreground position, blocked fraction is area(Dstar∩Dplanet)/π in these units: zero for d≥1+k, k² for d≤1−k, and the disk-intersection area during ingress/egress. This supplies continuous partial overlap without invented box-shaped measurements.

Orbital calculation: With negligible Mp, Kepler gives a/AU=[0.63(P/365.25)²]^(1/3). For b, c, candidate respectively: a=0.05251722, 0.08140862, 0.11907490 AU. Label “Model-derived approximate distances”. Preserve radius ratios 1:1.55013194:2.26734965 and angular-speed ratios 1:0.51813986:0.29290194. Drive all phases from the same illustrative clock, θj=2πt/Pj+θ0j. Phase offsets and coplanarity are illustrative; eccentricities and mutual orbital normals are not established here. Label overview body sizes exaggerated; restore exact k in closeup. Period ratios 1.92998084 and 1.76898744 do not establish resonances. The candidate orbit is dashed and labeled “candidate”, never “d”.

Duration consistency: In a circular model, A=a/Rstar, b=A cos i and T14=(P/π)asin[√((1+k)²−b²)/(A sin i)]. Using Rstar=0.60 Rsun gives A=42.6748874, illustrative i=88.9971598°, and T14=2.419808 h. The repository fit reports 2.45559074 h and Rp=2.207(+0.112,−0.108) Rearth. Keep fitted values distinct from the rounded stellar model; do not force simultaneous agreement. The fitted duration with the median k,b would imply A≈42.05328 under this circular relation. Neither constructed inclination is a measured orbital normal.

Optional directional belt: Let e1,e2 span an orbital plane and n be its normal. Observer directions permitting overlap satisfy |n·s|≤(Rstar+Rp)/a. Parameterize a sphere belt B(λ,β)=L[cos β(cos λ e1+sin λ e2)+sin β n], λ∈[0,2π], β∈[−α,α], α=asin[(Rstar+Rp)/a]. Candidate α≈1.38811°; b/c approximately 3.151°/2.037°. Larger a narrows the belt. Any visible enlargement must say “Widened schematic belt”. This is geometry, not a probability of candidacy.

Search logic: For known planet j define wrapped time Δj(t)=((t−t0j+Pj/2) mod Pj)−Pj/2. Mask samples satisfying |Δj|<wj around b/c transits before searching retained samples. Exact mask widths are unavailable in these snapshots; schematic windows must not imply measured widths. Do not subtract dips or interpolate gaps. Folding retained timestamps by the candidate period aligns hypothetical repetitions. A spatial bead strand represents time samples schematically, never sky position or raw photometry. The pinned README reports recovery as the strongest remaining signal by the separate TOI-host search; this is another search, not independent telescope data. [Repository snapshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/eumemic/exoplanets/ec8311b19a61092ad5eae3d34e947b14485d363e/README.md).

Evidence and limits: Eight points represent sectors [13,27,66,67,93,101,102,103], not eight transits; LEO reports nine. Old/new SNRs are 11.3393/7.39005. Nearest listed capable contaminator: 38.248 arcsec. The README reports none within 30 arcsec bright enough to mimic the dip. Centroid offsets 7.1,15.5,9.5 arcsec in S66/S67/S93 do not establish complete localization. Eclipsing blends, grazing binaries, aliases and systematic errors remain relevant traps; repetition alone is insufficient.

Use Gaia-constrained ten-run FPP_mean=0.1113498 and NFPP_max=1.1854×10⁻⁵ from triceratops_gaia.json, superseding README’s 0.14. Low neighboring-source probability does not eliminate target-associated false positives. FPP is conditional on tested models and priors, not detection confidence. Published validation criteria require FPP<0.015 and NFPP<0.001; the FPP requirement fails. [Giacalone et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.00691).

Pacing and conclusion: 0–10 s reverse tree; 10–25 light/area; 25–39 projection; 39–54 orbital rhythm; 54–70 masking/recovery; 70–85 evidence; 85–94 unresolved root and follow-up. At most one main formula and two caption lines simultaneously; other formulas above are implementation mathematics. Use stable modest meshes, depth-revealing moves and reading holds. The film derives conditional geometric relationships and illustrates the inference process; it neither proves a third planet nor uses topology as evidence. End: “A candidate. Confirmation still needed.” Ground photometry tests source location, high-resolution imaging constrains blends, and RVs test dynamical consistency.
checks: Read brief.json and all six immutable source artifacts; provenance identifies commit ec8311b19a61092ad5eae3d34e947b14485d363e, retrieved 2026-10-12.
Opened both requested primary papers, the pinned repository README, the primary transit-geometry paper and the TRICERATOPS validation paper.
Executed Python numerical checks for Kepler distances, radius/speed ratios, inclination, circular duration, belt angles and the ten-run FPP mean.
Independently integrated the planetary silhouette using 200,000 midpoint strips: 1141.7238026285 ppm, differing from k² by 0.00000396 ppm.

Inspected installed Manim 0.20.1 metadata and source for Surface, ParametricFunction, DashedVMobject, fixed labels and ThreeDScene camera methods. Surface supports explicit domains/resolution; move_camera supports orientation, zoom and frame_center.
Manim-environment runtime execution was denied. No runtime or render success is claimed. No files were edited and no work was delegated.
